title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9–11 of the manuscript): Grothendieck is setting up the combinatorial description of the boundary of M_{g,ν}. He works with an 'open' curve X = X̂ \ I. Here X̂ is a complete curve whose only singularities are ordinary double points, and its irreducible components are smooth (the previous page rules out loops). I is a finite set of marked points in the smooth locus of X̂. X̃ is the normalization and Y_α = X̂̃_α are the components of the compactified normalization.

Top of page: he finishes a realizability remark. Any finite graph without loops, with prescribed genera g_α at the vertices and a prescribed map I → S, arises from such a curve. One takes smooth curves of the given genera, glues them along the edges, and places the points of I on the smooth locus of the appropriate components.

Definition (10), the 'maquette' (combinatorial type) of a 'courbe standard' X, has three parts:
(a) The graph G_X = (S, Ã, σ_Ã). The vertex set is S = π_0(X̃) = π_0(X̂̃). Ã is the set of half-edges (oriented edges), i.e. the points of the normalization lying over the singular points. σ_Ã is the fixed-point-free involution exchanging the two branches at a node, so edges are Ã/σ = Sing(X).
(b) The finite set I = X̂ \ X of punctures, with its map I → S assigning each puncture to its component.
(c) The genus function g : S → ℕ, α ↦ genus of Y_α.

The last lines begin to abstract this: a structure formed by a finite graph G = (S, Ã, σ_Ã), a finite set I over the vertex set, and a 'genus' map S → ℕ.

In modern language this is exactly the stable (or modular) graph: vertices with genus labels, half-edges with an involution, and legs. It indexes the boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification of M_{g,ν}. The next page derives π_0(G_X) ≅ π_0(X) and the arithmetic-genus formula g = Σ g_α + h_1(G).
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The realizability claim is correct for any finite loopless graph with genus labels and legs; this is a construction, and no stability condition is imposed at this point.

Minor: the image appears to describe Ã via Sing(X) (possibly Sing of the normalization). Strictly, Ã should be the preimage of Sing(X) in X̃ (the half-edges); Sing(X) itself is the edge set Ã/σ. The notation is ambiguous in the manuscript.
On the next page (not this one), formula (14) as transcribed reads card S + card A + 1. It should be card A − card S + 1 = h_1(G).

ideas.what: Dual graph of a nodal curve with smooth components, encoded as vertices S = π_0 of the normalization, half-edges Ã = preimages of nodes, and the involution σ_Ã.
ideas.modern_name: dual graph / graph as half-edges with involution (Serre's oriented-edge formalism, flags)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969 for dual graphs of stable curves; Serre (Trees, 1977) for the edge-involution formalism; Kontsevich–Manin 1994 for the flag formalism in moduli
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the stratification of M̄_{g,ν} combinatorially, but not this explicit definition

ideas.what: 'Maquette': the triple (dual graph, legs I → S, genus map g : S → ℕ) as the combinatorial type of a pointed nodal curve.
ideas.modern_name: stable graph / modular graph (combinatorial type of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen, Deligne–Mumford; formalized by Kontsevich–Manin (1994) and Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)

ideas.what: Every finite loopless graph with genus labels and legs is realized by a curve with smooth components.
ideas.modern_name: nonemptiness of boundary strata for every combinatorial type

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard (if independently formulated) definition of the dual/stable graph of a pointed nodal curve, using the half-edge-plus-involution encoding. The only mildly notable points are the term 'maquette' and the early use of the half-edge formalism. Both are well established in the later literature (Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov), so a specialist would not be surprised.
transcription_corrections: 'courbe stable[?]' (twice) is more plausibly 'courbe standard', Grothendieck's term here for a curve with ordinary double points and smooth components.
'Une structure forme[?] d'un graphe' should read 'Une structure formée d'un graphe fini G ...'.
Under Ã the image appears to read 'Sing(X)'. The second line under the graph, π_0(X̂̃), belongs to the identification of S (S = π_0(X̃) = π_0(X̂̃)). A third symbol under σ_Ã is crossed out.
First line: 'Courbes X_α de genre g_α donné (i.e. des X̃_α de genre g_α ...)'. The g_α is an interlinear insertion above 'genre'.
'De plus, prenant ...' is likely 'De plus, quand on se donne I → S (I ens. fini)'.
